e-485.knowledge_point: Integrating a Quotient of Linear Polynomials
e-485.worked_solution:
The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder. For this, we can use synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

|  | $x^1$ | $x^0$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\color{red}-1$ | $4$ | $-1$ |
|  | $\color{gray}\downarrow$ | $-4$ |
|  | $4$ | $-5$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\dfrac{4x-1}{x+1} = 4 -\dfrac{5}{x+1}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{4x-1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4-\frac{5}{x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4\,\text{d}x-5{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4x{|}_{0}^{1}-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[4-0]-5[\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1] \\  & =4-5\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

e-486.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator is Linear
e-486.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division. 

We draw up a synthetic division table:

|  | $x^2$ | $x^1$ | $x^0$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\color{red}3$ | $2$ | $-3$ | $-4$ |
|  | $\color{gray}\downarrow$ | $6$ | $9$ |
|  | $2$ | $3$ | $5$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac{ 2x^2-3x-4}{x-3} = 2x + 3 + \dfrac {5}{x-3} .
	}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2{x}^{2}-3x-4}{x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2x+3+\frac{5}{x-3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}+3x+5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

e-487.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator Contains a Leading Coefficient
e-487.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $2$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x-1}{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x-1}{2(x-\frac{1}{2})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{x-1}{(x-\frac{1}{2})}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | $x^1$ | $x^0$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\color{red}\dfrac12$ | $1$ | $-1$ |
|  | $\color{gray}\downarrow$ | $\dfrac12$ |
|  | $1$ | $-\dfrac12$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-1}{(x-\frac{1}{2})} & =1-\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{(x-\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{2(x-\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{2x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x-1}{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int (1-\frac{1}{2x-1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[x-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-1|]+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate ∫3x−2x+1dx.

a
3x−3ln⁡|x+1|+C
b
3x−ln⁡|x+1|+C
c
3x+ln⁡|x+1|+C
d
3x+2ln⁡|x+1|+C
e
3x−5ln⁡|x+1|+C

decision.explanation: Since 3x-2=3(x+1)-5, the integrand is 3-5/(x+1). Integrating gives 3x-5\ln|x+1|+C, which is option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder. For this, we can use synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -1 & 3 & -2 \\  & ↓ & -3 \\  & 3 & -5\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{3x-2}{x+1}=3-\frac{5}{x+1}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3x-2}{x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3-\frac{5}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3x-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate ∫3x−2x+1dx.

a
3x−3ln⁡|x+1|+C
b
3x−ln⁡|x+1|+C
c
3x+ln⁡|x+1|+C
d
3x+2ln⁡|x+1|+C
e
3x−5ln⁡|x+1|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder. For this, we can use synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

xx0−13−2↓−33−5

So from the synthetic division, we get that

3x−2x+1=3−5x+1.

Therefore,

∫3x−2x+1dx=∫(3−5x+1)dx=3∫dx−5∫1x+1dx=3x−5ln⁡|x+1|+C.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Quotient of Linear Polynomials
content.worked_solution:
The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder. For this, we can use synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -1 & 3 & -2 \\  & ↓ & -3 \\  & 3 & -5\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{3x-2}{x+1}=3-\frac{5}{x+1}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3x-2}{x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3-\frac{5}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3x-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{8x+1}{x+3}=8-\frac{23}{x+3}.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{8x+1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{2}^{4}(8-\frac{23}{x+3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{\int }_{2}^{4}\text{d}x-23{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8x\,{|}_{2}^{4}-23\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|\,{|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =8(4-2)-23(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4+3|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|2+3|) \\  & =16-23(\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) \\  & =16-23\operatorname{ln}⁡(\,\frac{7}{5}\,).\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ -5 & 1 & 7 & 10 \\  & ↓ & -5 & -10 \\  & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+10}{x+5}=x+2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+10}{x+5}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+2)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1}+2x{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}]+2[1-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+2 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Calculate ∫3x3−9x2+x−1x−3dx.

a
x3−9x2+x+ln⁡|x−3|+C
b
13x3−3x2+2x−ln⁡|x−3|+C
c
13x3−3x−2ln⁡|x−3|+C
d
13x3−92x2+12x−3ln⁡|x−3|+C
e
x3+x+2ln⁡|x−3|+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Polynomial division gives (3x³-9x²+x-1)/(x-3)=3x²+1+2/(x-3). Integrating yields x³+x+2\ln|x-3|+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 3 & 3 & -9 & 1 & -1 \\  & ↓ & 9 & 0 & 3 \\  & 3 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{3{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+x-1}{x-3}=3{x}^{2}+1+\frac{2}{x-3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+x-1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3{x}^{2}+1+\frac{2}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+\int \text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{3}+x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Calculate ∫3x3−9x2+x−1x−3dx.

a
x3−9x2+x+ln⁡|x−3|+C
b
13x3−3x2+2x−ln⁡|x−3|+C
c
13x3−3x−2ln⁡|x−3|+C
d
13x3−92x2+12x−3ln⁡|x−3|+C
e
x3+x+2ln⁡|x−3|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

x3x2x1x033−91−1↓9033012

So from the synthetic division, we get that

3x3−9x2+x−1x−3=3x2+1+2x−3.

Therefore,

∫3x3−9x2+x−1x−3dx=∫(3x2+1+2x−3)dx=3∫x2dx+∫dx+2∫1x−3dx=x3+x+2ln⁡|x−3|+C.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator is Linear
content.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 3 & 3 & -9 & 1 & -1 \\  & ↓ & 9 & 0 & 3 \\  & 3 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{3{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+x-1}{x-3}=3{x}^{2}+1+\frac{2}{x-3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+x-1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3{x}^{2}+1+\frac{2}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+\int \text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{3}+x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

Evaluate the following integral:
∫03x2+8x+7x+4dx=
−9ln⁡(
)

decision.explanation: Polynomial division gives (x²+8x+7)/(x+4)=x+4-9/(x+4). Evaluating [x²/2+4x-9\ln|x+4|] from 0 to 3 gives 33/2-9\ln(7/4).

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder. For this, we can use synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

|  | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-4$ | $1$ | $8$ | $7$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-4$ | $-16$ |
|  | $1$ | $4$ | $-9$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+8x+7}{x+4}=x+4-\frac{9}{x+4}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}+8x+7}{x+4}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(x+4-\frac{9}{x+4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}x\,\text{d}x+4{\int }_{0}^{3}\text{d}x-9{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{0}^{3}+4x\,{|}_{0}^{3}-9\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|\,{|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({3}^{2}-{0}^{2})+4(3-0)-9(\operatorname{ln}⁡|3+4|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0+4|) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}+12-9(\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡4) \\  & =\frac{33}{2}-9\operatorname{ln}⁡(\,\frac{7}{4}\,).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

∫x3−2x2+3x−6x−2dx=

a
13x3−6x−3ln⁡|x−2|+C
b
x3−2x2+C
c
x3−ln⁡|x−2|+C
d
13x3+3x+C
e
13x3−x2+32x−6ln⁡|x−2|+C
Submit

decision.explanation: The numerator factors as (x-2)(x²+3), so the integrand is x²+3 for x≠2. Integrating gives x³/3+3x+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 3 & -6 \\  & ↓ & 2 & 0 & 6 \\  & 1 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+3x-6}{x-2}={x}^{2}+3.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+3x-6}{x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\int ({x}^{2}+3)\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+3\int \text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+3x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

∫x3−2x2+3x−6x−2dx=

a
13x3−6x−3ln⁡|x−2|+C
b
x3−2x2+C
c
x3−ln⁡|x−2|+C
d
13x3+3x+C
e
13x3−x2+32x−6ln⁡|x−2|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

x3x2x1x021−23−6↓2061030

So from the synthetic division, we get that

x3−2x2+3x−6x−2=x2+3.

Therefore,

∫x3−2x2+3x−6x−2dx=∫(x2+3)dx=∫x2dx+3∫dx=13x3+3x+C.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator is Linear
content.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 3 & -6 \\  & ↓ & 2 & 0 & 6 \\  & 1 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+3x-6}{x-2}={x}^{2}+3.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+3x-6}{x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\int ({x}^{2}+3)\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+3\int \text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+3x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

a

b

decision.explanation: Since (x+1)/(4x+1)=1/4+(3/4)/(4x+1), integrating gives x/4+(3/16)\ln|4x+1|+C. The factor 1/4 from integrating 1/(4x+1) makes option b correct.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $4$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x+1}{4(x+\frac{1}{4})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{4})}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{4} & 1 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{4} \\  & 1 & \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{4})} & =1+\frac{(\frac{3}{4})}{(x+\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =1+\frac{3}{4(x+\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =1+\frac{3}{4x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\int (1+\frac{3}{4x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\int \text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[x+\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+1|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{4}+\frac{3}{16}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{4} & 1 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{4} \\  & 1 & \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{4})} & =1+\frac{(\frac{3}{4})}{(x+\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =1+\frac{3}{4(x+\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =1+\frac{3}{4x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\int (1+\frac{3}{4x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\int \text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[x+\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+1|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{4}+\frac{3}{16}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Since 8x-1=2(4x-3)+5, the integrand is 2+(5/4)/(x-3/4). Integrating gives 2x+(5/4)\ln|x-3/4|+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $4$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8x-1}{4x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{8x-1}{4(x-\frac{3}{4})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{8x-1}{(x-\frac{3}{4})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ \frac{3}{4} & 8 & -1 \\  & ↓ & 6 \\  & 8 & 5\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8x-1}{(x-\frac{3}{4})} & =8+\frac{5}{(x-\frac{3}{4})}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8x-1}{4x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\int (8+\frac{5}{x-\frac{3}{4}})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[8\int \text{d}x+5\int \frac{1}{x-\frac{3}{4}}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[8x+5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-\frac{3}{4}|]+C \\  & =2x+\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-\frac{3}{4}|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Calculate ∫8x−14x−3dx.

a
 x4+14ln⁡|x−34|+C
b
 x4−14ln⁡|x−34|+C
c
 x+54ln⁡|x−34|+C
d
 2x+54ln⁡|x−34|+C
e
 2x−14ln⁡|x−34|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we pull out the factor of 4 from the denominator:

∫8x−14x−3dx=∫8x−14(x−34)dx=14∫8x−1(x−34)dx.

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

xx0348−1↓685

So from the synthetic division, we get that

8x−1(x−34)=8+5(x−34)

Therefore,

∫8x−14x−3dx=14∫(8+5x−34)dx=14[8∫dx+5∫1x−34dx]=14[8x+5ln⁡|x−34|]+C=2x+54ln⁡|x−34|+C.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator Contains a Leading Coefficient
content.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $4$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8x-1}{4x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{8x-1}{4(x-\frac{3}{4})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{8x-1}{(x-\frac{3}{4})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ \frac{3}{4} & 8 & -1 \\  & ↓ & 6 \\  & 8 & 5\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8x-1}{(x-\frac{3}{4})} & =8+\frac{5}{(x-\frac{3}{4})}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8x-1}{4x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\int (8+\frac{5}{x-\frac{3}{4}})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[8\int \text{d}x+5\int \frac{1}{x-\frac{3}{4}}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[8x+5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-\frac{3}{4}|]+C \\  & =2x+\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-\frac{3}{4}|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $3$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4x-5}{3x-2}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4x-5}{3(x-2/3)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4x-5}{(x-2/3)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{2}{3}$ | $4$ | $-5$ |
|  | $↓$ | $\frac{8}{3}$ |
|  | $4$ | $-\frac{7}{3}$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x-5}{(x-2/3)} & =4-\frac{(7/3)}{(x-2/3)} \\  & =4-\frac{7}{3x-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4x-5}{3x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}(4-\frac{7}{3x-2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[4{\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}x-7{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{3x-2}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[4x-\frac{7}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x-2|]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[4(3-1)-\frac{7}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|7|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[8-\frac{7\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{3}] \\  & =\frac{8}{3}-\frac{7}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡(7).\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The integrand equals 1/3+(2/3)/(6x+1). Evaluating its antiderivative x/3+(1/9)\ln|6x+1| from -1/12 to 0 gives 1/36+(1/9)\ln(2)=(1+4\ln(2))/36, matching option d.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $6$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6(x+\frac{1}{6})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{6})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{6} & 2 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{3} \\  & 2 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{6})} & =2+\frac{(\frac{2}{3})}{(x+\frac{1}{6})} \\  & =2+\frac{4}{6x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}(2+\frac{4}{6x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\text{d}x+4{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[2x+\frac{4}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+1|]}_{-1/12}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[2x+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+1|]}_{-1/12}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2(0-(-\frac{1}{12}))+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|6(0)+1|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|6(-\frac{1}{12})+1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2(\frac{1}{12})+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}))] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\frac{1}{6}+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2] \\  & =\frac{1}{36}(1+4\operatorname{ln}⁡2).\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $6$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6(x+\frac{1}{6})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{6})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{6} & 2 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{3} \\  & 2 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{6})} & =2+\frac{(\frac{2}{3})}{(x+\frac{1}{6})} \\  & =2+\frac{4}{6x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}(2+\frac{4}{6x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\text{d}x+4{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[2x+\frac{4}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+1|]}_{-1/12}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[2x+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+1|]}_{-1/12}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2(0-(-\frac{1}{12}))+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|6(0)+1|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|6(-\frac{1}{12})+1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2(\frac{1}{12})+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}))] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\frac{1}{6}+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2] \\  & =\frac{1}{36}(1+4\operatorname{ln}⁡2).\end{aligned}
$$
